value: P. copri encompasses four distinct clades (A, B, C, D) with >10% inter-clade genetic divergence
Analysis of 6,874 publicly available metagenomes from 36 datasets across 6 continents and 25 countries
1,023 P. copri genomes reconstructed: 17 isolate sequences and 1,006 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs)
Nearly ubiquitous prevalence (95.4%) in non-Westernized populations vs. 29.6% in Westernized populations
61.6% of non-Westernized individuals harbor all four clades; multi-clade co-presence is typical
Ancient metagenomes analyzed: Iceman (5,300-year-old) and pre-Columbian Mexican coprolites (1,300 ± 100 BP)
P. copri clade divergence estimated to pre-date human migration out of Africa (90-194 ka)
Substantial functional diversity in carbohydrate metabolism across clades
No strong evidence of clade association with disease (colorectal cancer, type 2 diabetes, IBD, hypertension, liver cirrhosis)

extraction_warnings: Paper focuses on metagenomic analysis of P. copri genomes rather than individual participant-level data. Individual subject_id and sample_id values are not provided in the paper. The paper reports aggregate cohort statistics for Ghana (44 individuals), Ethiopia (50 individuals), Tanzania (68 individuals), and Madagascar (110 individuals), but does not provide per-sample identifiers.

Detailed per-sample metadata (age, sex, family relationships) are reported only at cohort level summaries in the Methods section, not as individual sample rows. For Ghana: 23 adults (avg 33.14 yrs, 52.2% female) and 25 children (avg 6.81 yrs); Ethiopia: 24 adults (avg 29.35 yrs, 100% female) and 26 infants (avg 1.31 yrs); Tanzania: 37 adults (avg 29.27 yrs, 48.65% female) and 31 children (avg 8.22 yrs).

Family sampling was conducted in Ghana and Tanzania (extended families) and Ethiopia (mother-infant pairs), but individual family identifiers and per-sample family role assignments are not provided in the paper.

The paper reports that some samples were included in disease association analyses (CRC, T2D, hypertension, IBD) from other published datasets, but these are secondary data not generated in this study. Primary cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Madagascar) are described as healthy individuals.

Sample-level data for ancient samples (Iceman and Mexican coprolites) exist but are not appropriate for the standard sample schema as they represent archaeological specimens from distinct historical time periods rather than modern human subjects.
Batch 1 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

This paper is a metagenomic population genomics study of Prevotella copri across multiple cohorts (healthy and disease-associated). It does not contain individual-level clinical phenotype data, treatment responses, or biomarker measurements that would populate most of the requested schema fields. The schema appears designed for clinical trial or patient outcome studies; this paper analyzes microbial genetic diversity and prevalence patterns across geographic/lifestyle populations rather than individual patient outcomes.

Paper is a metagenomics study characterizing P. copri population structure and genetic diversity, not a clinical trial or interventional study; many clinically-focused schema fields are not applicable.
Study analyzed data from both newly sequenced cohorts and publicly available datasets; some cohort-level metadata varies across different datasets analyzed.
Ancient samples analyzed but not part of modern cohort demographics; different sequencing platforms used for ancient vs. modern samples.
Disease association analysis included multiple diseases (CRC, T2D, IBD, hypertension, liver cirrhosis) but found no strong clade-specific associations.
